summary: Lori Meeks specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She earned her BA at Columbia and PhD at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. She held a postdoc at Stanford (~2004–2005) before joining the University of Southern California in ~2005.

Lorna Srimathie Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London (~1963–1966), later serving as Associate Professor of History at the University of Ceylon and faculty at the University of Colombo (~1978).

A scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, Lothar Ledderose studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Tokyo, Princeton, Harvard, and Cologne. He served as Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and was President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

Specializing in archaeology and Sinology, Lothar von Falkenhausen studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard (MA ~1979–1982, PhD ~1982–1988). He taught at UC Riverside (~1991–1993) and became a professor at UCLA in 1993.

Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss at the Institut d'ethnologie. He held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford University (1951–1955), and the EHESS/EPHE from 1955.

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, Louis Finot studied at the École Nationale des Chartes. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1892–1898), directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1898, and taught at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 1980.

Louis Gernet worked in history and archaeology after studying at the École Normale Supérieure (~1902–1905). He held academic posts at the University of Algiers (~1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1948–1962).

A linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne, Louis Havet served as professor and Latin philology chair at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Herbert Gray was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton and Columbia (PhD ~1896–1900), and held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

Louis Komjathy specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Boston University under Paul Rouzer and served as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego (attested 2014).

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at the EPHE. He held posts at the University of Lyon (~1925–1937), EPHE (~1928–1966), University of Paris (~1937–1966), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1954–1956).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Louis de La Vallée Poussin studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden. He held Sanskrit chairs at Liège (1891–1892) and Ghent University (1893–1929).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Sinology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He was Chief Keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale (~1795–1824) and administrator and Persian chair at INALCO from 1795 to 1824.

Louise A. Cort specializes in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College, Oxford, and served as curator of ceramics at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from ~1981 to 2020.

Louise Child works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, studied under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at Leeds.
Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma (attested 1999).
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from ~1978 to 1983 and held a post there around 1993.
